title: Rython and R code integration
text:
This page was created following the guidelines from UBC MDS DSCI 521 milestone3 .


We use the Palmer Penguins dataset which is loaded via R library palmerpenguins and used by R and Python together.



First step, we use R to load the pengiuin data set and check what it has.

library(reticulate)
# py_config()
library(tidyverse)
library(palmerpenguins)
head(penguins)

# A tibble: 6 × 8
  species island    bill_length_mm bill_depth_mm flipper_length_mm body_mass_g
  <fct>   <fct>              <dbl>         <dbl>             <int>       <int>
1 Adelie  Torgersen           39.1          18.7               181        3750
2 Adelie  Torgersen           39.5          17.4               186        3800
3 Adelie  Torgersen           40.3          18                 195        3250
4 Adelie  Torgersen           NA            NA                  NA          NA
5 Adelie  Torgersen           36.7          19.3               193        3450
6 Adelie  Torgersen           39.3          20.6               190        3650
# ℹ 2 more variables: sex <fct>, year <int>





Then we use Python to use the penguins object from R context and calculate the average bill length (mm) of Adelie pengiuns on Torgersen island.

from IPython.display import display
# use penguins from R context
penguins = r.penguins
display(penguins.describe())

       bill_length_mm  bill_depth_mm  ...   body_mass_g         year
count      342.000000     342.000000  ...  3.440000e+02   344.000000
mean        43.921930      17.151170  ... -1.248119e+07  2008.029070
std          5.459584       1.974793  ...  1.635055e+08     0.818356
min         32.100000      13.100000  ... -2.147484e+09  2007.000000
25%         39.225000      15.600000  ...  3.550000e+03  2007.000000
50%         44.450000      17.300000  ...  4.025000e+03  2008.000000
75%         48.500000      18.700000  ...  4.750000e+03  2009.000000
max         59.600000      21.500000  ...  6.300000e+03  2009.000000

[8 rows x 5 columns]

print("\n")
display(penguins.head())

  species     island  bill_length_mm  ...  body_mass_g     sex  year
0  Adelie  Torgersen            39.1  ...         3750    male  2007
1  Adelie  Torgersen            39.5  ...         3800  female  2007
2  Adelie  Torgersen            40.3  ...         3250  female  2007
3  Adelie  Torgersen             NaN  ...  -2147483648     NaN  2007
4  Adelie  Torgersen            36.7  ...         3450  female  2007

[5 rows x 8 columns]

pats = penguins.query("species == 'Adelie' and island == 'Torgersen'" )
bill_length_mean = pats['bill_length_mm'].mean()
bill_length_mean

np.float64(38.950980392156865)





Then we use R to access the object of ‘bill_length_mean’ defined in Python context and output its value.
round(py$bill_length_mean, 1)
The average bill length of Adelie pengiuns on Torgersen is 39 mm.




penguins |>
  drop_na(bill_length_mm) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = species, y = bill_length_mm, fill = species)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.6, width = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.4, size = 1.8) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 18, size = 3.5, color = "darkred") +
  labs(
    x = "Species",
    y = "Bill Length (mm)",
    title = "Bill Length Distribution by Species",
    subtitle = "Diamonds indicate the mean bill length for each species"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")







Figure 1: Distribution of bill length across penguin species.

title: R code integration
text:
This page was created following the guidelines from UBC MDS DSCI 521 milestone3 . The dataset is loaded via library palmerpenguins.


We use the Palmer Penguins dataset to demonstrate how to embed R code and its output into an HTML page via Quarto.



First, we load the penguin dataset and inspect its contents.

library(tidyverse)
library(palmerpenguins)

head(penguins)

# A tibble: 6 × 8
  species island    bill_length_mm bill_depth_mm flipper_length_mm body_mass_g
  <fct>   <fct>              <dbl>         <dbl>             <int>       <int>
1 Adelie  Torgersen           39.1          18.7               181        3750
2 Adelie  Torgersen           39.5          17.4               186        3800
3 Adelie  Torgersen           40.3          18                 195        3250
4 Adelie  Torgersen           NA            NA                  NA          NA
5 Adelie  Torgersen           36.7          19.3               193        3450
6 Adelie  Torgersen           39.3          20.6               190        3650
# ℹ 2 more variables: sex <fct>, year <int>


Now, let’s find the average bill length (mm) of Adelie penguins on Torgersen Island.

pgs <- penguins |> filter(species == 'Adelie' & island == 'Torgersen') |>
    select("bill_length_mm") |>
    map_dbl(mean, na.rm = TRUE)

The average bill length of Adelie penguins on Torgersen Island is 39 mm.
